title: Sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and acid rain
key_idea: Burning fuels that contain sulfur makes sulfur dioxide. The high temperatures in engines make nitrogen and oxygen from the air form oxides of nitrogen. Both gases dissolve in rain to cause acid rain and cause breathing problems.

sections.heading: Where sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen come from

blocks.text: Two more pollutants form when fuels burn. This section covers where each one comes from.

items: Fuels such as coal and diesel contain sulfur as an impurity.
When the fuel burns, the sulfur reacts with oxygen to form sulfur dioxide.
Sulfur impurities are removed from fuels such as petrol before they are burned.

blocks.label: Burning sulfur
where: S is sulfur, an impurity in the fuel.

items: Air is mostly nitrogen, and the fuel does not supply it.
Car engines work at high temperatures.
At these temperatures nitrogen from the air reacts with oxygen from the air.

blocks.label: Forming nitrogen dioxide in an engine
where: N₂ is nitrogen from the air.
NO₂ is nitrogen dioxide, an oxide of nitrogen.

diagram.alt: Four atmospheric pollutants compared by source and effect.
items: Carbon monoxide
Particulates
Sulfur dioxide
Oxides of nitrogen

values: Incomplete combustion: soot and unburned hydrocarbons
Nitrogen and oxygen from the air reacting at high temperature in engines
Toxic: stops the blood carrying oxygen

items: Sulfur dioxide comes from sulfur impurities in fuels.
Oxides of nitrogen come from nitrogen and oxygen in the air reacting at high temperature.
Particulates are a different pollutant: they cause global dimming.

blocks.text: Sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen dissolve in water in clouds and rain. The rain becomes acidic.

diagram.alt: Put the steps that form acid rain from sulfur in a fuel into order.
steps: The fuel burns and the sulfur impurity reacts with oxygen
Sulfur dioxide gas forms and is released into the atmosphere
Sulfur dioxide dissolves in rain water or clouds
The rain becomes acidic and falls as acid rain
Acid rain damages buildings, plants and water life

items: It reacts with limestone, so buildings and statues are eroded.
It corrodes metals, bridges and other structures.
It damages trees and plants.
It acidifies lakes, rivers and soil, and kills aquatic life.

blocks.text: Sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen cause respiratory problems in humans, such as asthma.

items: Sulfur dioxide dissolves in rain to form an acid, so rain becomes acidic.
Acid rain erodes limestone and kills plants and aquatic life.
Reducing the sulfur in fuel means less sulfur dioxide and less acid rain.

checks.q: Explain how oxides of nitrogen are formed in a car engine.
checks.a: Car engines work at high temperatures. At these temperatures nitrogen from the air reacts with oxygen from the air.

checks.q: Explain why sulfur impurities are removed from petrol before it is burned.
checks.a: When burned, sulfur forms sulfur dioxide. This causes acid rain and respiratory problems.

checks.q: Explain how reducing the sulfur in fuel reduces the erosion of limestone.
checks.a: Sulfur reacts with oxygen to form sulfur dioxide, so less sulfur dioxide is emitted. This means less acid rain, so less limestone reacts with acid.

checks.q: Name the pollutant that causes global dimming.

exam_phrases: sulfur reacts with oxygen to form sulfur dioxide
nitrogen (from air) reacts with oxygen (from air)

mistakes.wrong: Oxides of nitrogen form from impurities in the fuel.
mistakes.right: The nitrogen comes from the air. At the high temperature in the engine it reacts with oxygen from the air.
Particulates cause global dimming. Sulfur dioxide causes acid rain.

mistakes.wrong: The only problem caused by sulfur dioxide is acid rain.
mistakes.right: Sulfur dioxide also causes respiratory problems. A named problem such as asthma is allowed.

worked_example.question:
Fossil fuels are burned in car engines.

Explain how reducing the amount of sulfur in fossil fuels reduces the erosion of limestone.
answer_points: Sulfur reacts with oxygen to form sulfur dioxide.
So less sulfur dioxide is emitted.
So there is less acid rain.
So less limestone reacts with the acid rain.
worked_example.tip: Each mark is one link in the chain, so write the steps in order.

exam_phrases: sulfur / S (is present as an impurity)
sulfur dioxide dissolves in rain / water / clouds

mistakes.right: Name the gas as sulfur dioxide, SO₂. Sulfur oxide is ignored.

mistakes.wrong: Sulfur dioxide mixes with rain to make acid rain.
mistakes.right: Mixes with is ignored. Say sulfur dioxide dissolves in or reacts with rain, water or clouds.
The equation is not balanced and scores only one mark. Balance it: N₂ + 2O₂ → 2NO₂.

worked_example.question:
Acid rain is caused by some pollutant gases present in the atmosphere.

Explain how impurities in fossil fuels can result in acid rain.
answer_points: Sulfur is present as an impurity in the fuel.
When the fuel burns, the sulfur reacts with oxygen (is burned or oxidised).
Sulfur dioxide dissolves in rain, water or clouds.
worked_example.tip: Any three of these points score. S + O₂ → SO₂ scores the first three.

exam_phrases: erosion of stonework / corrosion of metals
kills trees or kills living things in rivers or lakes

mistakes.right: References to pollution are ignored. Say that it causes acid rain, and give an effect such as eroding stonework.

mistakes.wrong: Carbon monoxide is harmful or dangerous.
mistakes.right: Harmful and dangerous are ignored. Say it is poisonous or toxic.

worked_example.question:
Petrol is a mixture of hydrocarbons obtained from crude oil.
When petrol burns in a car engine the exhaust gases contain nitrogen monoxide, NO, and carbon monoxide, CO.
These are atmospheric pollutants.

Describe one environmental problem for each gas.

NO ______
CO ______
answer_points: NO: causes acid rain. An effect such as erosion of stonework, corrosion of metals, or killing trees or river life is also allowed.
CO: poisonous or toxic. An effect such as difficulty breathing or reducing the oxygen the blood can carry is also allowed.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each gas. Contributing to global warming is ignored.
